text:
emma: Heads-up — Acorn Health on a private VPC deployment can't complete the installer. Errors when downloader hits model registry and telemetry: TLS verify failed + some DNS lookups time out. Can neteng/devon take a look? cc @neteng @devon

devon: Thanks. Can you paste the exact installer output? Also which region/VPC?

emma: Pasted from their run (redacted):
```
ERROR: fetch model manifest: https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/manifest: curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.local' does not match target host name 'model-registry.redwood.ai'
caused by: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
DNS lookup for telemetry.redwood.ai timed out after 5s
```

leo: Looks like outbound TLS intercept + DNS split-horizon. If their corporate proxy is resigning certs, installer will fail unless we teach the box to trust the proxy CA or bypass intercept for our hosts.

neteng: Agreed. Two quick repro checks for their infra to run (share with customer):
1) DNS check:
```
dig +short model-registry.redwood.ai
dig +short telemetry.redwood.ai
```
2) TLS handshake/subject check:
```
openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -showcerts
curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/manifest
```
If the `openssl` cert subject CN shows `proxy.local` or their proxy hostname, they have TLS intercept.

emma: I also have a short curl capture they ran: `curl -v https://telemetry.redwood.ai/health` returns `* SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-proxy' does not match target host name 'telemetry.redwood.ai'`

devon: For firewall/egress allowlist, ask them to permit these hosts and ports (outbound TCP 443):
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- artifactory.redwood.ai
- s3.amazonaws.com (for some model storage endpoints; region-specific buckets)
- cdn-models.redwood.ai
Also allow: IP ranges for AWS regions they use (if they block by IP).

leo: Additional notes: if they run a TLS-terminating proxy, options are:
- Configure the proxy for SNI passthrough for `*.redwood.ai` (preferred)
- Add the proxy CA to the OS trust store on installer hosts (if allowed)
- Use a network rule to bypass the proxy for those hostnames

support-ops: One more gotcha — some proxies rewrite OCSP responses. If they see `OCSP_RESPONSE: malformed` we usually ask them to skip OCSP stapling interception or allow our OCSP endpoints.

neteng: For a minimal allowlist entries we normally provide a sample that customers can paste into firewall configs. Requested customer to run `traceroute -n telemetry.redwood.ai` to confirm egress path.

emma: Customer ran `dig` and got two different answers from internal vs public resolver. They have split-horizon DNS returning internal IPs that are unreachable from installer. They say the internal IPs are for a deprecated CDN.

devon: If split-horizon is returning internal-only addresses, installer will try to connect to private IP and fail. Ask them to point hosts to public DNS for those FQDNs or add DNS forwarders to resolve public records. Alternatively add static /etc/hosts entries mapping to the public IPs we return from our public resolver (temporary workaround).

leo: Example troubleshooting commands we gave them to confirm TLS & DNS: 
```
# public lookup
dig +short model-registry.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
# compare to local resolver
dig +short model-registry.redwood.ai
# test TLS SNI
openssl s_client -connect $(dig +short model-registry.redwood.ai | head -n1):443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai
```

emma: They asked for a canonical list of endpoints to whitelist. I drafted this — please review before I send: (they wanted hostnames only)
- model-registry.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- artifactory.redwood.ai
- cdn-models.redwood.ai
- s3-<region>.amazonaws.com (replace <region> as needed)
- time.cloudflare.com (for NTP via CDN)

devon: Looks good. Add `ocsp.digicert.com` and `crl.pki.goog` if their proxy validates OCSP/CRL. Also call out TCP/443 and optionally TCP/80 for redirects.

neteng: I'll add a short note about certificates: if they must intercept TLS, they should either: 
1) Add the proxy root CA to the OS and Docker trust stores where installer runs, OR
2) Configure the proxy to allow TLS passthrough for `*.redwood.ai`, `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, and `artifactory.redwood.ai`.

support-ops: Pasting a minimal troubleshooting checklist for the customer to run (they can paste in support ticket):
```
1) dig +short telemetry.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8 && dig +short telemetry.redwood.ai
2) openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai
3) curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/v1/manifest
4) traceroute -n telemetry.redwood.ai
5) check proxy CA in /etc/ssl/certs or `update-ca-certificates` equivalent
```

emma: I'll send the checklist + allowlist. Customer also asked about whether we require long-lived allowlist entries for S3 buckets — they do some narrow egress rules by hostname only.

devon: We recommend allowing the S3 hostnames for the region(s) they expect model pulls from (we can share exact bucket names if they open a case with account info). If they cannot allow S3, we offer a packaged mirror option for enterprise installs (requires support).

leo: One-off note: if they get `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`, they should run `openssl x509 -in /path/to/proxy-ca.pem -noout -text` and confirm that CA is present; if running via Docker, ensure `update-ca-trust` is done inside the container image as well.

emma: Great — I'll send this to Acorn and ask them to run the checklist. Will follow up here after they reply. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Installer v2.3 run for Acorn Health recorded (run-id: r-7a9b). Logs attached to support ticket #AC-1382.

emma: thanks — closing loop for now, will reopen if they still see failures.
